findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Apache Web Server (3186) defines `apache:access:combined`, `apache:access:kv` and `apache:access:json`, and extracts CIM-style fields (`http_referrer`, `http_user_agent`, `src`, `url`). `access_combined` is Splunk's built-in pretrained sourcetype, so the fields the SPL uses come from core access-extractions, not the add-on. A reader who follows the app/implementation advice and assigns the add-on's sourcetype will get a search that returns nothing.
findings.quote: Apache combined access logs in `index=web` with `sourcetype="access_combined"` (TA-parsed fields: `clientip`, `useragent`, `referer`, `uri`, `status`, `bytes`)
findings.suggested_fix: Say the SPL relies on Splunk's built-in `access_combined` sourcetype and needs no add-on. Alternatively, if Splunk_TA_apache is used with `apache:access:combined`, state that the field names differ (http_referrer, http_user_agent, src, url). Align app, implementation and the inputs.conf example with that choice.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Channel is assigned per hit rather than per session, and the site's own hostname is not excluded from referers. Every internal page view (referer = own site) therefore falls into 'Referral'. Then `stats first(epv) ... by session_id channel` splits one session into several channel rows, each carrying the whole session's page count, so sessions and pageviews are double-counted and Referral dominates the share. Derive channel from the first hit of each session (for example `eventstats first(channel) by session_id` after sorting by _time) and treat own-domain referers as internal.

The social regex `t\\.co` is unanchored, so it matches any referer containing 't.co' (for example microsoft.com, reddit.com, *soft.com). Those visits are mis-tagged as 'Social — ref'. Anchor the match on ref_host (for example `^t\\.co$`).

Only favicon/robots/health are excluded, so CSS/JS/image/font requests are counted as pages. This inflates pages_per_session and suppresses bounce_rate. Including 3xx and 4xx in the status filter also counts 404s and redirects as pageviews.

The title promises 'SEO Performance', but the SPL only measures channel share from server logs; no Search Console impressions, rankings or queries are ingested. Consider 'Website Traffic Source Mix from Web Server Logs', or add a Search Console source.

summary: The detailedImplementation is detailed and specific to server-log channel classification, and the grandmaExplanation is good. However, the UC attributes the `access_combined` fields to the Apache add-on, which actually uses different sourcetypes. Its sessionisation counts internal navigation as 'Referral' traffic, so the channel shares are wrong. Exclusions, evidence and false positives are template residue.
